questions.text:
निम्नलिखित आँकड़ों (डाटा) के आधार पर किस प्रकार का पारिस्थितिक पिरैमिड प्राप्त होगा ?
प्राथमिक उत्पादक = 10 g
द्वितीयक उपभोक्ता = 120 g
प्राथमिक उपभोक्ता = 60 g
questions.text_english:
What type of ecological pyramid would be obtained with the following data ?
Primary producer = 10 g
Secondary consumer = 120 g
Primary consumer = 60 g
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Inverted pyramid of biomass. In the given data, the primary producer has the least biomass (10 g), primary consumer has more (60 g), and secondary consumer has the most (120 g). This means biomass increases at each successive trophic level, resulting in an inverted pyramid of biomass. Options A and D are incorrect because in a normal upright pyramid, biomass/energy decreases at each higher trophic level. Option B is about numbers, not biomass.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) जैवमात्रा का उलटा पिरैमिड है। दिए गए डाटा में प्राथमिक उत्पादक की जैवमात्रा सबसे कम (10 g) है, प्राथमिक उपभोक्ता की अधिक (60 g) और द्वितीयक उपभोक्ता की सबसे अधिक (120 g) है। इस प्रकार प्रत्येक उच्च पोषण स्तर पर जैवमात्रा बढ़ती है, जिससे जैवमात्रा का उलटा पिरैमिड बनता है।

questions.text: ऐसे पुष्य जिनमें अंडाशय में केवल एक ही बीजांड होता है और पुष्पक्रम में अनेक पुष्पगुच्छ होते हैं, उनका परागण सामान्यत: इस कारक द्वारा होता है :
questions.text_english: Flowers which have single ovule in the ovary and are packed into inflorescence are usually pollinated by
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Wind. Flowers with a single ovule in the ovary packed into inflorescences are typically wind-pollinated (anemophilous). Wind-pollinated flowers produce large amounts of light, non-sticky pollen that can be carried by air currents to other flowers. They do not need to attract pollinators, so they lack attractive features like bright colours or nectar. Water, bat, and bee pollination are associated with different floral characteristics.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) वायु है। जिन पुष्पों में अंडाशय में केवल एक बीजांड होता है और जो पुष्पक्रम में होते हैं, वे सामान्यत: वायु परागित (वायुपरागी) होते हैं। वायु परागित पुष्पों में बड़ी मात्रा में हल्के, गैर-चिपचिपे पराग कण होते हैं।

questions.text:
नीचे दिए गए चित्र में एक द्विबीजपत्री भ्रूण के विकास के चरणों को दर्शाया गया है। इसके चार भागों को 'P', 'Q', 'R' तथा 'S' द्वारा नामांकित किया गया है।
भ्रूण विकास के विभिन्न चरणों में 'P', 'Q', 'R' तथा 'S' के सही नामांकन वाले विकल्प को चुनिए :
questions.text_english:
The diagram given below shows labelling of four parts of a dicot embryo during its development as P, Q, R and S.
Choose the option that indicates correct labelling of 'P', 'Q', 'R' and 'S' of embryo in different stages of its development :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) P-Zygote, Q-Suspensor, R-Cotyledon, S-Radicle. In dicot embryo development, the fertilized egg first forms a zygote (P). The zygote divides to produce a suspensor (Q) and the embryo proper. As development proceeds to the heart-shaped stage, cotyledons (R) become visible. In the mature embryo, the radicle (S) is clearly differentiated. Options A and C are wrong as P is zygote, not egg. Option B is incorrect as R is cotyledon, not plumule at that stage.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। द्विबीजपत्री भ्रूण विकास में निषेचित अंड पहले युग्मज (P) बनाता है। युग्मज विभाजित होकर निलंबक (Q) और भ्रूण उत्पन्न करता है। हृदयाकार अवस्था में बीजपत्र (R) विकसित होते हैं। परिपक्व भ्रूण में मूलांकुर (S) स्पष्ट दिखता है।

questions.text: आधुनिक मानव के विकास में निम्नलिखित मानव सदृश नर वानर गण (प्राइमेट्स) सम्मिलित हैं। मानव विकास के सही अनुक्रम वाले विकल्प को चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Evolution of modern man involves the following man-like primates. Choose the correct series of human evolution.

options.A: ड्रायोपिथेकस → होमो इरैक्टस → ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो सैपियंस
options.B: ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो इरैक्टस → नियंडरथल → होमो सैपियंस
options.D: होमो इरैक्टस → ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो सैपियंस → नियंडरथल

options_english.A: Dryopithecus → Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens
options_english.B: Australopithecines → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
options_english.D: Homo erectus → Australopithecines → Homo sapiens → Neanderthal

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Australopithecines → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens. This is the accepted sequence of human evolution. Australopithecines were the earliest hominids, followed by Homo erectus who first used fire and migrated out of Africa. Neanderthals coexisted with early Homo sapiens and eventually became extinct. Options A, C and D place the primates in incorrect chronological sequences.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। मानव विकास का सही क्रम है: ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन → होमो इरैक्टस → नियंडरथल → होमो सैपियंस। ओस्ट्रेलोपिथेसिन सबसे प्रारंभिक होमिनिड थे, फिर होमो इरैक्टस आए जिन्होंने पहली बार अग्नि का उपयोग किया।

questions.text: एक व्यक्ति जिसके पिता वर्णांध थे, एक ऐसी स्त्री के साथ विवाह करता है जिसकी माता वर्णांध तथा पिता सामान्य दृष्टि वाले थे। इस युगल के कितने प्रतिशत पुत्र वर्णांध होंगे ?
questions.text_english: A man whose father was colour-blind marries a woman who had a colour-blind mother and normal father. What percentage of male children of this couple will be colour-blind ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 50%. The man's father was colour-blind, so the man received X^b Y from his parents, making him X^B Y (normal vision as he is not colour-blind). The woman's mother was colour-blind (X^b X^b) and father was normal (X^B Y), so the woman is a carrier: X^B X^b. Cross: X^B Y (father) × X^B X^b (mother). Sons will be X^B Y (normal) or X^b Y (colour-blind) in equal proportion, i.e., 50% colour-blind sons.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) 50% है। पुरुष के पिता वर्णांध थे, अत: पुरुष X^B Y है। महिला की माता वर्णांध (X^b X^b) और पिता सामान्य (X^B Y) थे, इसलिए महिला वाहक X^B X^b है। क्रॉस से 50% पुत्र X^b Y (वर्णांध) होंगे।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस समूह में भ्रूण के विकास (परिवर्धन) की अवधि में ही भ्रूणपोष पूर्णत: उपभुक्त कर लिया जाता है। सही विकल्प चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo in which of the following ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Pea and Groundnut. In non-endospermic (exalbuminous) seeds such as pea and groundnut, the endosperm is completely consumed by the developing embryo during seed maturation, and nutrients are stored in the cotyledons. In contrast, maize is an endospermic seed where endosperm persists in the mature seed. Castor is also endospermic. Hence options A, B and C are incorrect.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) मटर तथा मूंगफली है। ये अभ्रूणपोषी (नॉन-एंडोस्पर्मिक) बीज हैं जिनमें भ्रूण के विकास के दौरान भ्रूणपोष पूरी तरह उपभुक्त हो जाता है और पोषक तत्व बीजपत्रों में संग्रहीत होते हैं।

questions.text: 'जी ई ए सी' का पूरा नाम है :
questions.text_english: GEAC stands for
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. GEAC is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India. It is responsible for approving activities involving large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and for approving field experiments of genetically modified organisms (GMOs). The other options are incorrect full forms fabricated to confuse.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग एप्रूवल कमेटी है। GEAC भारत सरकार के पर्यावरण एवं वन मंत्रालय के अंतर्गत एक वैधानिक निकाय है जो आनुवंशिक रूप से संशोधित जीवों के क्षेत्र परीक्षण को अनुमोदित करती है।

questions.text: कुछ रोगियों में ऊतक/अंग प्रत्यारोपण अकसर रोगी के ऊतकों/अंगों द्वारा अस्वीकृत किए जाने के कारण असफल हो जाता है। इस प्रकार की अस्वीकृति के लिए उत्तरदायी प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया का प्रकार है :
questions.text_english: Transplantation of tissues/organs to some patients often fails due to rejection of such tissues/organs by the body of the patient. Which type of immune response is responsible for such rejections ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Cell mediated immune response. Graft rejection following organ transplantation is primarily mediated by T-lymphocytes (T-cells), which is a cell-mediated immune response. The T-cells recognize the foreign MHC (major histocompatibility complex) antigens on the transplanted tissue and mount an immune attack. Humoral immunity involves antibodies, while autoimmune response is directed against self-antigens. Physiological immune response is not a standard immunological term.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) कोशिका माध्यित प्रतिरक्षा अनुक्रिया है। अंग प्रत्यारोपण अस्वीकृति मुख्यत: T-लिम्फोसाइट्स द्वारा होती है। T-कोशिकाएं प्रत्यारोपित ऊतक पर विदेशी MHC प्रतिजनों को पहचानकर प्रतिरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया करती हैं।

questions.text: डी एन ए पॉलीमरेज का उपयोग करते हुए लाभकारी जीन को लगभग _______ गुना तक प्रवर्धित किया जा सकता है।
questions.text_english: Amplification of gene of interest by using DNA polymerase may go upto
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1 billion times. In the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), the gene of interest can be amplified up to approximately 1 billion (10^9) times using thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase). Each PCR cycle doubles the number of copies, and after about 30 cycles, one gets approximately 2^30 ≈ 1 billion copies. Options A, B, and D are either too low or too high.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) 1 बिलियन है। पॉलीमरेज चेन रिएक्शन (PCR) में ताप-स्थिर DNA पॉलीमरेज (Taq पॉलीमरेज) का उपयोग करके लाभकारी जीन को लगभग 1 बिलियन (10^9) गुना तक प्रवर्धित किया जा सकता है।

questions.text:
आरएनए अंतरक्षेप (RNAi) तंबाकू के पौधे को सूत्रकृमि (मेलॉइडोजिन इनकोगनीशिया) के प्रति प्रतिरोधी बनाने में सहायक है।
उचित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिससे ज्ञात हो सके कि आरएनए अंतरक्षेपी किस प्रकार प्राप्त किया जाता है :
questions.text_english:
RNA interference (RNAi) helps in making tobacco-plant resistant to a nematode (Meloidegyne incognita)
Choose the correct option that shows how RNAi is achieved :

options.A: सूत्रकृमि के एमआरएनए के रूपांतरण प्रक्रम का अवरोधन।
options.B: सूत्रकृमि के डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन को अवरोधित करना।
options.C: पौधे के डीएनए के अनुलेखन को अवरोधित करना।
options.D: पौधे के डीएनए के प्रतिकृतीयन को अवरोधित करना।

options_english.A: Preventing the process of translation of mRNA of the nematode.
options_english.B: Preventing the process of replication of DNA of the nematode.
options_english.C: Preventing the process of transcription of DNA of the plant.
options_english.D: Preventing the process of replication of DNA of the plant.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Preventing the process of translation of mRNA of the nematode. In RNAi, nematode-specific complementary dsRNA is introduced into the tobacco plant via Agrobacterium. When the nematode feeds on the plant, the dsRNA enters the nematode and silences the specific mRNA of the nematode through the RISC complex, preventing its translation. This effectively kills the nematode. Options B, C, and D describe wrong mechanisms.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। RNAi में, नेमाटोड-विशिष्ट dsRNA तंबाकू पौधे में प्रविष्ट कराया जाता है। जब नेमाटोड पौधे को खाता है, तो dsRNA उसमें प्रवेश कर RISC कॉम्प्लेक्स द्वारा उसके mRNA के रूपांतरण को रोकता है।

questions.text:
एक डीएनए खंड की कोडिंग रज्जु में नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों का अनुक्रम 5' – AATGCTAGGCAC – 3' है।
इस डीएनए द्वारा अनुलेखित 'm-आरएनए' में नाइट्रोजनी क्षारकों का सही अनुक्रम दर्शाने वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: The sequence of nitrogenous bases in a segment of a coding strand of DNA is 5' – AATGCTAGGCAC – 3'. Choose the option that shows the correct sequence of nitrogenous bases in the mRNA transcribed by the DNA.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 5' – AAUGCUAGGCAC – 3'. The mRNA is transcribed from the template strand, which is complementary and antiparallel to the coding strand. The mRNA sequence is identical to the coding strand but with U replacing T. The coding strand is 5'-AATGCTAGGCAC-3', so the mRNA will be 5'-AAUGCUAGGCAC-3' (replacing T with U). Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they do not follow the simple T-to-U replacement rule.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 5' – AAUGCUAGGCAC – 3' है। mRNA कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड के समान अनुक्रम का होता है, केवल T के स्थान पर U होता है। कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड 5'-AATGCTAGGCAC-3' है, अत: mRNA 5'-AAUGCUAGGCAC-3' होगा।

questions.text: जब YyRr पौधे को जीनों के लिए अप्रभावी जनक के साथ बैककॉस कराने के परिणाम का सही विकल्प कौन सा होगा ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is correct for the condition when plant YyRr is back crossed with the double recessive parent ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 1:1:1:1 ratio of phenotypes and genotypes. When YyRr is crossed with the double recessive parent yyRr — wait, the double recessive is yyrr. YyRr × yyrr produces four genotypes: YyRr, Yyrr, yyRr, yyrr in a 1:1:1:1 ratio. Since each genotype is unique and each produces a distinct phenotype, both phenotypic and genotypic ratios are 1:1:1:1. The 9:3:3:1 ratio is obtained from a dihybrid cross (F2), not a test/back cross.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। YyRr × yyrr (टेस्टक्रॉस) से चार जीनोटाइप YyRr, Yyrr, yyRr, yyrr 1:1:1:1 अनुपात में बनते हैं। प्रत्येक जीनोटाइप का अलग फीनोटाइप होता है, इसलिए फीनोटाइप तथा जीनोटाइप दोनों का अनुपात 1:1:1:1 होता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : नवजात शिशु के पोषण के लिए स्तन ग्रंथियाँ दुग्धस्रवण करती हैं।
कारण (R) : यह रूपांतरित स्वेद ग्रंथियाँ हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The mammary glands secrete milk for the nourishment of the young ones.
Reason (R) : These are modified sweat glands.
questions.instruction_line: Both (A) and (R) are given. Select the correct option.
questions.instruction_line_english:
For Questions number 13 to 16 two statements are given - one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Answer these questions by selecting the appropriate option given below:
(A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(B) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(C) (A) is true, but (R) is false.
(D) (A) is false, but (R) is true.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). The Assertion is correct: mammary glands do secrete milk to nourish the young ones. The Reason is also correct: mammary glands are indeed modified sweat glands that have evolved to produce milk instead of sweat. The Reason correctly explains the Assertion because their evolutionary origin as sweat glands explains their secretory nature and capacity to produce milk.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन सत्य है - स्तन ग्रंथियाँ दुग्ध स्रावित करती हैं। कारण भी सत्य है - ये रूपांतरित स्वेद ग्रंथियाँ हैं। कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है क्योंकि स्वेद ग्रंथि की उत्पत्ति उनकी स्रावी प्रकृति की व्याख्या करती है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : पाड़ (स्केफोल्ड) प्रोटीन गैर-हिस्टोन गुणसूत्रीय प्रोटीन हैं।
कारण (R) : वे लाइसीन तथा आर्जिनिन समृद्ध होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Scaffold proteins are non-histone chromosomal proteins.
Reason (R) : They are rich in lysine and arginine.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या हो रही है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R) द्वारा (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं हो रही है।

questions.text_english:
Study the two different crosses given below :
[Cross I: Parents 44+XX × 44+XY; Gametes 22+O, 22+XX, 22+X, 22+Y; Offspring 1]
[Cross II: Parents 44+XY × 44+XX; Gametes 22+Y, 22+X, 23+X, 21+X; Offspring 2]
Identify the abnormalities '1' and '2' in the offsprings of given crosses and distinguish between them.

key_points: Offspring 1 from Cross I: 22+O gamete from mother × 22+X gamete from father = 44+XO = Turner's syndrome
Offspring 2 from Cross II: 22+X (normal) from father × 23+X (non-disjunction) from mother = 44+XXX (Triple X) or 22+Y × 23+X = 44+XXY = Klinefelter's syndrome
Turner's: female, 45 chromosomes, sterile, short stature; Klinefelter's: male, 47 chromosomes, gynaecomastia, sterile

questions.solution: Offspring 1 (Cross I) results from the 22+O maternal gamete fusing with the 22+X paternal gamete, giving 44+XO — this is Turner's syndrome. The individual is a phenotypic female with only 45 chromosomes, short stature, rudimentary ovaries, and is sterile. Offspring 2 (Cross II) results from 22+X (father) fusing with 23+X (mother, due to non-disjunction) giving 44+XXY — this is Klinefelter's syndrome. The individual is a phenotypic male with 47 chromosomes, gynaecomastia, and is sterile. The key difference is Turner's (XO, female, 45 chromosomes) versus Klinefelter's (XXY, male, 47 chromosomes).

questions.solution:
Option (A): Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is chemically derived from morphine by acetylation using acetic anhydride. Both are opiates that act on the central nervous system. They bind to opioid receptors in the brain, causing euphoria, pain relief, sedation, and respiratory depression. Prolonged use leads to severe physical and psychological dependence. Morphine is used medically as a painkiller, while heroin has no accepted medical use and is highly addictive.

Option (B): (i) Alcoholic drinks with distillation: Whisky, Rum, Brandy. Without distillation: Wine, Beer. (ii) Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc can fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia through the enzyme nitrogenase. When used as bio-fertilizers in paddy fields, they enrich the soil with nitrogen, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers and improving soil fertility.

Student to attempt either option-(A) or (B) :
(A) Analyse the following ecosystems and discuss which will be more productive in terms of primary productivity :
A young forest, a natural old forest, a shallow polluted lake.
OR
(B) Differentiate between Net primary productivity and Gross primary productivity in an ecosystem.
questions.instruction_line: विकल्प-(A) अथवा (B) में किसी एक का उत्तर लिखिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Student to attempt either option-(A) or (B).

key_points: Option A: Young forest is most productive in primary productivity; old forest has lower NPP as respiration equals photosynthesis
Option B: GPP = total photosynthesis; NPP = GPP minus respiration losses

questions.solution:
Option (A): A young forest is the most productive in terms of primary productivity. In a young forest, plants are actively growing and photosynthesis far exceeds respiration, resulting in high net primary productivity (NPP). In a natural old forest, the ecosystem is in a climax state where photosynthesis roughly equals respiration, so NPP approaches zero. A shallow polluted lake has very low primary productivity due to reduced light penetration caused by turbidity and pollution.

Option (B): Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total rate of photosynthesis (total energy fixed by autotrophs) in an ecosystem per unit time and area. Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the energy remaining after autotrophs have used some for their own respiration (R). Thus, NPP = GPP - R. NPP represents the biomass available for consumers and is always less than GPP.

Student to attempt either option-(A) or (B) :
(A) A patient with ADA deficiency requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes. Explain why such periodic infusion is required and also suggest a permanent cure for such ADA deficiency.
OR
(B) Describe in brief any two techniques that can be utilised to transfer recombinant DNA into the host cell directly without using any vector.
questions.instruction_line: विकल्प 'A' अथवा 'B' में से किसी एक का उत्तर लिखिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Student to attempt either option-(A) or (B).

key_points: Option A: Engineered lymphocytes are not immortal; they die off so periodic infusion is needed; permanent cure is gene therapy via introducing ADA gene into bone marrow stem cells
Option B: Microinjection - DNA injected directly into nucleus; Biolistics/Gene gun - DNA coated gold particles shot into cells

questions.solution:
Option (A): The genetically engineered lymphocytes infused into the ADA patient are not immortal. They have a finite lifespan and die after some time. Since the patient lacks the ADA gene in their own cells, no new functional lymphocytes are produced. Therefore, periodic infusions are required to maintain a sufficient number of functional lymphocytes. A permanent cure would be gene therapy: introducing the functional ADA gene into the patient's bone marrow stem cells so that all subsequent lymphocytes derived from those stem cells will carry the ADA gene permanently.

Option (B): Two techniques to transfer recombinant DNA without a vector are: (1) Microinjection — the recombinant DNA is directly injected into the nucleus of an animal cell using a fine glass needle (micropipette). (2) Biolistics (Gene gun) — DNA is coated onto microscopic gold or tungsten particles and bombarded into plant cells at high velocity using a gene gun.

questions.text_english: Compare and contrast convergent and divergent evolution.

key_points: Divergent evolution: common ancestor, structures are homologous, different functions
Convergent evolution: different ancestors, structures are analogous, similar functions
Examples: Divergent - forelimbs of whale, bat, horse; Convergent - wings of butterfly and bird

questions.solution: Divergent evolution occurs when organisms sharing a common ancestor evolve different characteristics due to adaptation to different environments. The resulting structures are homologous — they have the same basic structure and origin but serve different functions, such as the forelimbs of humans, whales, bats, and horses. Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated organisms independently evolve similar traits due to similar environmental pressures. The resulting structures are analogous — they have similar functions but different origins and internal structures, such as the wings of insects and birds, or the eyes of octopus and vertebrates. In summary, divergent evolution leads to homology (same origin, different function) while convergent evolution leads to analogy (different origin, same function).

श्याम तथा राधा अपनी प्रथम संतान की प्रतीक्षारत हैं क्योंकि राधा दो मास से गर्भवती है और कोई जटिलता भी नहीं है। श्याम के परिवार में पुटीय तंतुमयता का इतिहास है तथा राधा के परिवार में डाउंस सिंड्रोम का पारिवारिक इतिहास है। इसलिए चिंता है कि शिशु को इनमें से कोई एक विकार होने की संभावना है।
(a) ऐसे किसी तरीके का सुझाव दीजिए जिससे गर्भस्थ भ्रूण के वंशागत विकार का परीक्षण किया जा सके। उस तकनीक की व्याख्या कीजिए।
(b) यदि किसी एक अथवा दोनों विकारों की उपस्थिति पता चलती है तथा माँ के स्वास्थ्य को खतरा हो तो उनके लिए किसी एक संभावित विकल्प का उल्लेख कीजिए। राधा की वर्तमान गर्भावस्था के लिए क्या यह विकल्प सुरक्षित होगा ? न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए।
(c) किन परिस्थितियों में उप-प्रश्न (b) में सुझाया गया विकल्प अवैधानिक है ?
questions.text_english:
Shyam and Radha are expecting their first child with Radha being in her second month of pregnancy with no complications. Shyam's family has a history of cystic fibrosis while Radha's family has a history of Down's syndrome, leading to a concern that the baby may have one of these conditions.
(a) Suggest and explain a way of testing if their baby is at risk for any genetic disorders.
(b) In case of presence of one or both of the abnormalities and posing a risk to the mother's health, mention one possible option for them to consider. Is that option safe for Radha at the current gestational age ? Justify.
(c) Under what conditions is the process mentioned in (b) illegal ?

key_points: (a) Amniocentesis or CVS — fetal cells collected and karyotyped/tested
(b) Medical termination of pregnancy (MTP); at 2 months it is safe as MTP is legal up to 20 weeks
(c) MTP is illegal if done for sex determination/sex-selective abortion

questions.solution:
(a) Amniocentesis can be used to test the foetus for genetic disorders. In this technique, a small sample of amniotic fluid (containing foetal cells) is withdrawn from the uterus using a syringe. The foetal cells are then cultured and their chromosomes are examined (karyotyping) to detect chromosomal abnormalities like Down's syndrome (trisomy 21). DNA analysis can also be done to detect gene mutations like cystic fibrosis.

(b) If one or both abnormalities are detected and pose a risk to the mother's health, Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is a possible option. Since Radha is only in her second month (about 8 weeks), MTP is safe. As per the MTP Act in India, termination is legal up to 20 weeks of gestation with medical advice. At 2 months, the procedure carries minimal risk.

(c) MTP is illegal when it is performed for sex-selective purposes, i.e., to terminate a female foetus identified through prenatal sex determination. Under the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, sex determination leading to sex-selective abortion is a criminal offence.
questions.solution_hindi:
(a) एम्नियोसेंटेसिस तकनीक का उपयोग किया जा सकता है। इसमें एम्नियोटिक द्रव से भ्रूण कोशिकाएं प्राप्त की जाती हैं और गुणसूत्रीय असामान्यताएं जांची जाती हैं।
(b) MTP (चिकित्सीय गर्भ समापन) एक विकल्प है। 2 माह की गर्भावस्था में यह सुरक्षित है क्योंकि MTP अधिनियम के अनुसार 20 सप्ताह तक MTP कानूनी है।
(c) MTP तब अवैध है जब इसे लिंग चयन हेतु (कन्या भ्रूण हत्या के लिए) किया जाए। PCPNDT अधिनियम के तहत यह अपराध है।

questions.text_english:
(a) Write the palindromic nucleotide sequence for following sequence of DNA segment :
5' – GAATTC – 3'
(b) Name the restriction endonuclease that recognizes this sequence.
(c) How are sticky ends produced ? Mention their role.

key_points: (a) 5'-GAATTC-3' / 3'-CTTAAG-5' (complementary strand reads same 5'to3')
(b) EcoRI
(c) Sticky ends are single-stranded overhangs produced by staggered cuts; they help in joining DNA fragments by complementary base pairing

questions.solution:
(a) The palindromic sequence for 5'-GAATTC-3' is:
5'-GAATTC-3'
3'-CTTAAG-5'
This is a palindrome because the complementary strand read in the 5' to 3' direction also gives GAATTC.

(b) The restriction endonuclease that recognizes the sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' is EcoRI (isolated from Escherichia coli RY13).

(c) Sticky ends are produced when a restriction enzyme makes a staggered cut (not a straight cut) in the two strands of the double-stranded DNA. EcoRI cuts between G and A on both strands but at slightly offset positions, leaving short single-stranded overhangs — these are sticky ends. Their role is to facilitate the joining of two DNA fragments: the complementary sticky ends from different fragments can base-pair with each other, allowing DNA ligase to covalently join them to form recombinant DNA.
questions.solution_hindi:

5'-GAATTC-3'
3'-CTTAAG-5'
(b) इस अनुक्रम को पहचानने वाला एंजाइम EcoRI है।
(c) चिपचिपे छोर तब बनते हैं जब प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम दोनों स्ट्रैंड्स को स्थानांतरित (staggered) स्थानों पर काटता है, जिससे एकल-स्ट्रैंड के सिरे निकलते हैं। ये सिरे पूरक क्षारक युग्मन द्वारा अन्य DNA खंडों से जुड़ने में सहायता करते हैं।

questions.text_english:
Study a part of life cycle of Plasmodium given below :
Answer the following questions :
(a) Name the infective stage of Plasmodium that is stored in the female Anopheles mosquito.
(b) Where does fertilization and development of parasite take place ?
(c) Identify labels P and Q in the given diagram.
(d) Asexual and sexual phase of the life cycle of the Plasmodium takes place in two different hosts. Write their names.

key_points: (a) Sporozoites
(b) In the gut/stomach of female Anopheles mosquito
(c) P = Oocyst; Q = Sporozoites
(d) Asexual phase in humans; Sexual phase in female Anopheles mosquito

questions.solution:
(a) The infective stage of Plasmodium stored in the salivary glands of the female Anopheles mosquito is the sporozoite. When the mosquito bites a healthy human, sporozoites are injected into the bloodstream.

(b) Fertilization and development of the parasite (sexual phase) takes place in the gut (stomach) of the female Anopheles mosquito. The male and female gametocytes ingested during a blood meal fuse to form a zygote, which develops into an oocyst.

(c) P = Oocyst (the stage in the mosquito gut where the zygote develops); Q = Sporozoites (infectious units released from the oocyst that migrate to the salivary glands).

(d) The asexual phase (schizogony) of Plasmodium takes place in humans (the intermediate host), while the sexual phase (gametogony and sporogony) takes place in the female Anopheles mosquito (the primary/definitive host).

questions.text_english:
Study the diagram given below and answer the questions that follows :
(a) Identify the structure shown in the above figure.
(b) Identify the labels P and Q.
(c) Write the nature of histone proteins.
(d) Distinguish between Euchromatin and Heterochromatin.

key_points: (a) Nucleosome
(b) P = Histone octamer; Q = DNA double helix wrapped around histone
(c) Histones are basic (positively charged) proteins rich in lysine and arginine
(d) Euchromatin: loosely packed, transcriptionally active; Heterochromatin: tightly packed, transcriptionally inactive

questions.solution:
(a) The structure shown in the figure is a Nucleosome — the basic unit of chromatin packaging in eukaryotes.

(b) P = Histone octamer (made up of two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 histones); Q = DNA double helix that is wound around the histone octamer (approximately 200 base pairs per nucleosome).

(c) Histone proteins are basic (positively charged) in nature because they are rich in the positively charged amino acids lysine and arginine. This positive charge allows them to associate strongly with the negatively charged phosphate backbone of DNA.

(d) Euchromatin is the loosely packed, less condensed region of chromatin that stains lightly. It is transcriptionally active and contains genes that are actively expressed. Heterochromatin is the densely packed, highly condensed region that stains darkly. It is generally transcriptionally inactive and contains repetitive sequences.

questions.text_english:
(A) Who is having more species diversity — Columbia or Greenland and why ?
(B) Explain the concept proposed by Paul Ehlrich.

key_points: (A) Colombia has more species diversity because it lies in the tropics with warm, stable climate and high solar energy
(B) Paul Ehrlich proposed the Rivet Popper Hypothesis: like rivets in an airplane, each species plays a role; losing species (rivets) weakens the ecosystem

questions.solution:
(A) Colombia has greater species diversity than Greenland. Colombia is situated in the tropical region near the equator, which receives more solar energy, has a warm and stable climate, and provides a diverse range of habitats. These conditions favour high speciation rates and support a much greater variety of species. Greenland, located in the arctic region, has extreme cold, limited solar energy, and fewer niches, resulting in low biodiversity.

(B) Paul Ehrlich proposed the Rivet Popper Hypothesis to explain the importance of biodiversity. He compared an ecosystem to an airplane held together by rivets (species). Just as an airplane can lose a few rivets (species) without immediate danger, an ecosystem may lose a few species. However, as more and more rivets (species) are removed, the airplane (ecosystem) becomes increasingly vulnerable and may eventually collapse. This analogy illustrates that every species, no matter how insignificant it appears, contributes to ecosystem stability.
questions.solution_hindi:
(A) कोलम्बिया में जातिविविधता अधिक होती है क्योंकि यह उष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्र में स्थित है जहाँ अधिक सौर ऊर्जा, स्थिर जलवायु और विविध आवास होते हैं। ग्रीनलैंड आर्कटिक में है जहाँ ठंड अधिक है।
(B) पॉल एहलरिच की रिवेट पॉपर परिकल्पना: पारिस्थितिक तंत्र एक हवाई जहाज जैसा है जिसे रिवेट (जातियाँ) जोड़ते हैं। जातियों के विलुप्त होने से पारिस्थितिक तंत्र कमजोर होता जाता है और अंततः नष्ट हो सकता है।

questions.text_english:
(A) Differentiate between Recombinant DNA and cDNA.
(B) Explain the method to increase the competency of the bacterial cell membrane to take up recombinant DNA.

key_points: (A) Recombinant DNA: formed by joining DNA from two different sources; cDNA: synthesized from mRNA using reverse transcriptase, has no introns
(B) Treat bacteria with divalent cations (Ca2+) and heat shock at 42°C to make them competent to take up DNA

questions.solution:
(A) Recombinant DNA is formed by artificially combining DNA fragments from two different sources (e.g., a gene of interest inserted into a plasmid vector). It contains both the insert and the vector sequences and may contain introns. cDNA (complementary DNA) is synthesized in the laboratory from a mature mRNA molecule using the enzyme reverse transcriptase. It represents only the coding sequence of a gene (no introns, no non-coding regions) and is used when the gene is to be expressed in a prokaryote.

(B) To increase the competency of bacterial cell membranes to take up recombinant DNA, bacteria are treated with divalent cations such as calcium ions (Ca2+) by incubating them in ice-cold CaCl2 solution. This treatment temporarily makes the cell membrane more permeable to DNA. The bacteria are then briefly exposed to heat shock (42°C for 90 seconds) followed by rapid cooling. This heat shock creates a thermal imbalance that forces the DNA into the bacterial cell through the transiently permeable membrane.
questions.solution_hindi:
(A) पुनयोगज DNA: दो विभिन्न स्रोतों के DNA को मिलाकर बनाया जाता है, इसमें इंट्रॉन हो सकते हैं। c-DNA: mRNA से रिवर्स ट्रांसक्रिप्टेज द्वारा बनाया जाता है, इसमें इंट्रॉन नहीं होते।
(B) जीवाणु कोशिकाओं को कैल्शियम क्लोराइड (CaCl2) घोल में ठंडे तापमान पर रखा जाता है, फिर 42°C पर ताप आघात (heat shock) दिया जाता है। इससे कोशिका झिल्ली अस्थायी रूप से पारगम्य हो जाती है और पुनयोगज DNA कोशिका में प्रवेश कर जाता है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित परिच्छेद को पढ़कर अग्रगामी प्रश्नों के उत्तर लिखिए :
प्रकृति में, हमें किसी भी जाति के पृथक, एकल व्यक्ति के दर्शन विरले ही होते हैं; उनमें से अधिकांश सुपरिभाषित भौगोलिक क्षेत्र में समूह में रहते हैं। वे समान संसाधनों का साझा उपयोग करते हैं अथवा उनके लिए स्पर्धा करते हैं, संकरण करते हैं और इस प्रकार वे समष्टि की रचना करते हैं। समष्टि में कुछ ऐसे गुण होते हैं जो व्यष्टि जीव में नहीं होते। एक नियत समय में समष्टि में विभिन्न आयु वर्ग की व्यष्टियाँ होती हैं। किसी समष्टि का आकार उसके आवास में समष्टि की स्थिति के बारे में बहुत कुछ बताता है। समष्टि में हम कैसे भी पारिस्थितिक प्रक्रम अन्वेषण (इन्वेस्टिगेट) करना चाहें, भले ही यह दूसरी जातियों में स्पर्धा का परिणाम हो, परभक्षी का प्रभाव हो, या पीड़कनाशी (पेस्टीसाइड) अनुप्रयुक्त करने का प्रभाव हो, हम उनका मूल्यांकन हमेशा ही समष्टि के साइज में परिवर्तन के संदर्भ में करते हैं। प्रकृति में समष्टि का आकार (साइज) बहुत कम हो सकता है अथवा लाखों की संख्या में हो सकता है। समष्टि का आकार (साइज) तकनीकी रूप से समष्टि घनत्व (N) कहलाता है। परन्तु यह आवश्यक नहीं है कि उसे केवल संख्या के आधार पर ही मापा जाए। किसी समष्टि के लिए समष्टि का साइज एक निश्चल (स्थिर) प्राचल नहीं है। यह समय के साथ परिवर्तित होता रहता है जो अनेक कारकों भोजन की उपलब्धता, परभक्षण दाब तथा विपरीत मौसम पर निर्भर करता है।
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow :
In nature, we rarely find isolated, single individuals of any species; majority of them live in groups in a well-defined geographical area, share or compete for similar resources, potentially interbreed and thus constitute a population. The population has certain attributes whereas an individual organism does not. A population at a given time is composed of individuals of different ages. The size of the population tells us a lot about its status in the habitat. Whatever ecological processes we wish to investigate in a population, be it the outcome of competition with another species, the impact of the predator or the effect of pesticide application, we always evaluate in terms of any change in the population size. The size, in nature, could be low or go into millions. Population size, technically called population density (N) need not necessarily be measured in numbers only. The size of a population for any species is not a static parameter. It keeps on changing with time depending on various factors including food availability, predation pressure and adverse weather.

key_points: N(t) = N(t+1) - Natality - Immigration + Mortality + Emigration = 800 - 200 - 200 + 150 + 100 = 650
Since natality > mortality, population is growing — expanding pyramid (broad base)

sub_questions.solution:
Using the population growth formula: N(t+1) = N(t) + Natality - Mortality + Immigration - Emigration
800 = N(t) + 200 - 150 + 200 - 100
800 = N(t) + 150
N(t) = 800 - 150 = 650
The population density at time t is 650. Since natality (200) is greater than mortality (150) and immigration (200) exceeds emigration (100), the population is growing. This indicates an expanding (progressive) age pyramid with a broad base, indicating a large proportion of young individuals and a growing population.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the difference in a method of measuring population density in an area if there are 200 carrot grass plants to only single huge banyan tree ?

Banyan tree: measured by percentage cover or biomass, not numbers, as one tree may cover huge area

sub_questions.solution: For 200 carrot grass plants, population density is measured by directly counting the number of individuals per unit area (numerical density). However, for the single huge banyan tree, counting numbers would be misleading because one banyan tree can spread over a very large area with numerous aerial roots, making it appear as multiple individuals. In this case, population density is better expressed as percentage cover (the area covered by the tree canopy) or as biomass per unit area, which gives a more accurate representation of the organism's impact on the habitat.

sub_questions.solution: Two methods to measure the population density of tigers are: (1) Pugmark census (Pug mark method) — tiger paw prints (pugmarks) are collected, traced onto paper, and analyzed to identify individual tigers and estimate their numbers. (2) Camera trap method — motion-sensor cameras are set up in the forest to photograph tigers; each tiger is identified by its unique stripe pattern, allowing researchers to count individuals and estimate population density.

sub_questions.solution: The hormone responsible for the peak (surge) observed in both Case 1 and Case 2 is LH (Luteinizing Hormone), secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. sub_questions.solution: During the follicular phase, in the ovary: primary follicles mature and develop into Graafian follicles under the influence of FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) from the anterior pituitary. The growing follicles secrete increasing amounts of estrogen (estradiol). In the uterus: estrogen stimulates the proliferation and thickening of the endometrium (uterine lining) in preparation for potential implantation. The uterine glands increase in number and the blood supply to the endometrium improves.

sub_questions.solution: In Case 2 (which represents pregnancy), hormone Q is HCG — Human Chorionic Gonadotropin. HCG is secreted by the trophoblast cells of the developing embryo after implantation. One function of HCG: it maintains the corpus luteum during early pregnancy, preventing its degeneration. This ensures continued secretion of progesterone from the corpus luteum, which is essential to maintain the endometrium and support the developing embryo until the placenta takes over hormone production.

sub_questions.solution: In Case 2 (pregnancy), the corpus luteum remains functional for a prolonged period. In a normal cycle, the corpus luteum degenerates after about 10-12 days. However, in pregnancy, HCG secreted by the trophoblast maintains the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum is formed from the remnants of the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation. Under the influence of LH, the granulosa and theca cells of the ruptured follicle undergo luteinization — they enlarge and fill with yellow lipid droplets — forming the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone to sustain the pregnancy.

key_points: Option A(i): Test cross with double recessive (terminal white flowers); if all violet = homozygous; if 1:1 = heterozygous
Option A(ii): Haplodiploidy: males from unfertilized eggs (haploid, 16 chr); females from fertilized eggs (diploid, 32 chr)
Option B: DNA fingerprinting steps: isolation, restriction digestion, electrophoresis, Southern blotting, hybridization with probe, autoradiography, pattern comparison

questions.solution:
Option (A)(i): To determine the genotype of an axial, violet-flowered pea plant (both are dominant traits), a test cross is performed with a homozygous recessive plant having terminal, white flowers (genotype: aabb). If the plant is homozygous dominant (AABB), all offspring will show axial violet flowers. If the plant is heterozygous (AaBb), the offspring will show four phenotypes — axial violet : axial white : terminal violet : terminal white in a 1:1:1:1 ratio. Thus the genotype can be determined by observing the progeny.

Option (A)(ii): Haplodiploidy is the sex determination mechanism in honey-bees. Female honey-bees (queen and workers) develop from fertilized eggs and are diploid with 32 chromosomes. Male honey-bees (drones) develop from unfertilized eggs by parthenogenesis and are haploid with 16 chromosomes. Drones produce sperms by mitosis (not meiosis, since they are haploid). This system means males have no father but have a grandfather.

Option (B): DNA fingerprinting of blood samples R and S involves the following steps:
1. Isolation of DNA from blood samples R and S.
2. Digestion of DNA using specific restriction endonucleases to produce DNA fragments of varying sizes.
3. Gel electrophoresis to separate the DNA fragments by size.
4. Southern blotting — transferring separated fragments onto a nylon membrane.
5. Hybridization with a radioactively or fluorescently labelled probe that is complementary to the VNTR (Variable Number Tandem Repeat) sequences.
6. Autoradiography — exposing the membrane to X-ray film to visualize the banding pattern.
7. Comparison of the banding patterns of R and S with each other and with the suspect's DNA to establish identity.

questions.solution:
Option (A):
(i) MALT stands for Mucosa Associated Lymphoid Tissue. It constitutes about 50% of the lymphoid tissue in the human body and is located within the linings of the digestive, respiratory, and urogenital tracts. It forms the first line of immune defense at mucosal surfaces.

(ii) Cytokine barriers are a type of innate defense. When a cell is infected by a virus, it secretes small proteins called interferons (a type of cytokine). These interferons do not protect the infected cell itself but diffuse to neighbouring uninfected cells, stimulating them to produce antiviral proteins that prevent viral replication, thereby forming a protective barrier.

(iii) The diagnostic test for AIDS is ELISA (Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay). It works on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction. It detects HIV-specific antibodies in the patient's blood serum. If HIV antibodies are present, an enzyme-linked secondary antibody produces a colour change that can be quantified.

(iv) Bone marrow is the primary lymphoid organ where all blood cells, including lymphocytes, are produced (haematopoiesis). B-lymphocytes mature in the bone marrow itself. The thymus is another primary lymphoid organ where T-lymphocyte precursors (from bone marrow) migrate and undergo maturation and selection, becoming immunocompetent T-cells capable of immune responses.

Option (B)(i): H = Clostridium butylicum (bacterium); I = Bacterium; J = Statins (Lovastatin); K = Fungus; L = Trichoderma polysporum; M = Immunosuppressant (used in organ transplantation to prevent rejection).

(ii) Baculoviruses are used as biological control agents because they are species-specific — they attack only the target insect pest and do not harm other insects, plants, mammals, or birds. They are environmentally safe, cause no pollution, and are effective against specific agricultural pests like caterpillars and leaf-eating insects.

questions.solution:
Option (A)(a): In a mature male gametophyte (pollen grain) of an angiosperm, two cells are present: the vegetative cell (tube cell) and the generative cell. The vegetative cell is large, has a large irregular nucleus, and contains stored food. It forms the pollen tube. The generative cell is small, spindle-shaped, and divides mitotically to produce two male gametes (sperms) inside the pollen tube.

Option (A)(b)(i): Method 1 = Geitonogamy (transfer of pollen from one flower to another flower of the same plant); Method 2 = Xenogamy (cross-pollination — pollen transferred from a flower of one plant to a flower of a genetically different plant); Method 3 = Autogamy (self-pollination — pollen from the anther of a flower transferred to the stigma of the same flower).

(ii)(a) Water lily: Pollination is achieved by insects (entomophily). The flowers are colourful and fragrant to attract insects. (b) Vallisneria: Pollination is achieved on the water surface (epihydrophily). Female flowers are on long stalks that reach the water surface. Male flowers are released and float to the surface where they contact the female flowers.

(iii) Advantages of autogamy (method 3): Pollination is certain and does not depend on external agents. It preserves parental genotype as no cross-breeding occurs. It is advantageous when pollinators are scarce. Seed set is guaranteed.

Option (B)(i): Sperm Q successfully penetrates the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane of the ovum, achieving fertilization. Sperm P has already entered the perivitelline space (between zona pellucida and plasma membrane) but cannot fertilize because the cortical reaction has blocked further entry. Sperm R is still outside the zona pellucida and is unable to penetrate because polyspermy block has been established.

(ii) The zona pellucida plays two key roles: it induces the acrosome reaction in the sperm (release of acrosomal enzymes needed to penetrate it), and after fertilization by the first sperm, the cortical granules released by the ovum cause the zona reaction — the zona pellucida hardens and becomes impenetrable, thereby preventing polyspermy.

(iii) After sperm entry: the secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division, releasing the second polar body and forming the mature ovum. The chromosomes of the sperm and ovum form the male and female pronuclei respectively, which fuse (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote. The cortical reaction occurs — cortical granules beneath the plasma membrane fuse with it and release enzymes into the perivitelline space, hardening the zona pellucida to prevent polyspermy.

(iv) The acrosome (cap-like structure on the sperm head) contains hydrolytic enzymes such as hyaluronidase and acrosin. During the acrosome reaction, these enzymes are released and help the sperm penetrate the corona radiata and zona pellucida to reach the ovum. The middle piece of the sperm is packed with mitochondria that produce ATP by cellular respiration. This ATP provides the energy required for vigorous tail movements (flagellar beating) that propel the sperm through the female reproductive tract to reach and fertilize the ovum.

विकल्प (A)(a): परिपक्व नर युग्मकोद्भिद में दो कोशिकाएं होती हैं: कायिक कोशिका (बड़ी, पराग नलिका बनाती है) और जनन कोशिका (छोटी, दो नर युग्मक बनाती है)।

विकल्प (B)(i): Q शुक्राणु सफलतापूर्वक निषेचन करता है; P पेरिवाइटेलाइन अंतरिक्ष में है पर निषेचन नहीं कर सकता; R जोना पेलुसिडा के बाहर है।
(ii) जोना पेलुसिडा एक्रोसोम अभिक्रिया उत्प्रेरित करती है और कॉर्टिकल अभिक्रिया द्वारा बहुशुक्राणुता रोकती है।
(iii) द्वितीय अर्धसूत्री विभाजन पूर्ण, द्वितीय ध्रुवीय पिंड निर्मुक्त, कॉर्टिकल अभिक्रिया, युग्मनज निर्माण।
(iv) अग्रपिंडक: एंजाइम स्रावित करता है जो जोना पेलुसिडा भेदन में सहायक। मध्यखंड: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया से ATP उत्पन्न होती है जो पूंछ चलन के लिए ऊर्जा प्रदान करती है।
